title: NoRA: Evaluating Grounded Reasonableness in Visual First-person Normative Action Reasoning
abstract: arXiv:2606.04806v2 Announce Type: replace-cross  Abstract: LLMs and agentic systems are increasingly deployed in social environments, making normative competence critical for safe and appropriate behavior. However, existing approaches either assess normative judgment in text alone or reduce it to choosing among a fixed set of candidate actions. We argue both are insufficient. In practice, agents are never handed a menu of options; they must identify a reasonable action from scratch, grounded in visible facts and supported by inspectable reasons. We introduce NoRA, a visual first-person video benchmark that requires models to generate candidate next actions and justify each through an explicit fact-reason-action support graph. The benchmark comprises 1,420 annotated video clips, including HumanGold-190 and LLMSilver-1230 splits. translated_title: NoRA：在视觉第一人称规范性行动推理中评估有依据的合理性
translated_abstract: 大语言模型（LLM）和智能体系统正越来越多地被部署到社会环境中，这使得规范能力对于实现安全且恰当的行为变得至关重要。然而，现有方法要么仅在纯文本层面评估规范判断，要么将其简化为在一组固定的候选动作中进行选择。我们认为这两种方式都不充分。在实践中，智能体从不会被提供一份现成的选项菜单；它们必须从零开始识别出一个合理的行动，该行动应以可见的事实为依据，并由可检验的理由来支撑。我们提出了NoRA，一个视觉第一人称视频基准，要求模型自主生成候选的下一步行动，并通过显式的事实-理由-行动支持图对每个行动进行论证。该基准包含1,420个带标注的视频片段，包括HumanGold-190和LLMSilver-1230两个数据划分。每个实例通过行动对齐、事实依据和支持绑定三个维度进行评估，并汇总为一个单一的“有依据的合理性”分数。我们对多个模……
tldr: 提出NoRA第一人称视频基准，要求模型自主生成候选行动并通过显式的事实-理由-行动支持图加以论证，从行动对齐、事实依据和支持绑定三方面评估模型在有真实依据的规范性行动推理上的合理性。
en_tdlr: NoRA is a first-person video benchmark requiring models to generate candidate next actions from scratch and justify each via an explicit fact-reason-action support graph, evaluating grounded reasonableness in normative action reasoning.
